settings.title: Settings
settings.libraryLocaleHint: Switching UI language later will not rename folders on disk
settings.autoLaunchHint: Atrium must keep running in the tray to notice Unity starting
settings.libraryRootHint: Archive mode moves assets here and organizes them by category
settings.autoExtractHint: Off by default to save space. When enabled, extracted contents are saved too; combine with Keep original archives.
settings.detectVcc: Read from the ALCOM / VCC manifest
settings.rebuildHint: The lifesaver when the database is corrupt
settings.sevenZip: This program uses 7-Zip (by Igor Pavlov), distributed under the GNU LGPL.
settings.privacy: Privacy: apart from an LLM service you explicitly configure under Classification, this app makes no network requests. Your assets never leave this machine.
settings.llmWarn: When enabled, only the file list and description text of low-confidence assets are sent to the service you configured.
settings.libraryRootMissing: No library root set — ingest and archiving are unavailable
settings.bridgeAutoInstallHint: When on, projects seen for the first time — and any you answered "always install" for — get the bridge when they appear or Unity opens them. A toast reports what was copied; the project page can uninstall (to the Recycle Bin).
settings.watchedFoldersHint: New files are ingested automatically (3s debounce)
settings.watchedRunning: Watching {{count}} folder(s) — dropped files queue themselves
settings.contextMenuOff: Not registered yet. Register it to see the entry in Explorer's right-click menu.
settings.dictionaryHint: The built-in dictionary ships with the app and is read-only. Terms you add here win, and they affect the next classification immediately.
settings.userTermsHint: {{builtin}} built-in terms loaded. The ones below are yours and override built-ins on a name clash.
settings.termEmpty: Term and category are both required
settings.learnedRulesHint: Every time you fix a classification in the review queue, it keeps that clue. Deleting here makes it forget.
settings.learnedEmpty: Nothing learned yet — correct one classification and it shows up here.
settings.termUnknownCat: That category / subcategory combination does not exist
settings.autoArchiveHint: When off, every asset waits in Review no matter how confident we are — files only move when you confirm. Recommended for a first whole-library adoption.
settings.reclaimHint: Settings → Maintenance → library health scan → Re-register. It feeds unregistered folders into the ingest queue, so they still go through extract → classify → merge; nothing is frozen as-is.
settings.rebundleHint: The previous build split collections into flat assets. This scans read-only for “items that live in the same folder”, previews the merge, then re-attaches them: no files move, undoable with Ctrl+Z.
settings.rebundleWhyContainer: same folder, name is a container word
settings.regroupHint: Merging requires the same parent folder. Early versions grouped by merge key alone, gluing same-named items from different folders onto one card. This scans for those groups and re-splits them per folder: no file is moved, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
settings.regroupKeptTitle: {{count}} more groups stay merged (not a mis-merge)
settings.regroupKeptWhy: These are one product's archive plus its already-extracted copy sitting in two folders — by the agreed rule they stay a single card, so they were left alone.
settings.learnTitle: Learn model names from the library
settings.learnWhy: Scans file names of the form <model>_<series> and lists recurring names the lexicon does not know yet. Once added, similar assets merge automatically and detail pages can show model badges.
settings.learnNone: No new likely model names — the lexicon already covers this library
settings.learnThresholdNote: Only names seen ≥2 times within one series are listed; when a single series has 20 different models once each, the whole series group is listed (this is exactly the ATTITUDE The Royal Bunny case in the real library)
settings.reanalyzeWhy: After changing the naming / version / bracket-merge rules, names computed under the old rules need recomputing. This step **only updates database columns and moves no files**; it tells you how many rows are affected before you press it, and the whole batch can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
settings.reanalyzeAffected: {{scanned}} records in the library, {{affected}} would change
settings.reanalyzeUuid: {{count}} still carry a UUID in the name
settings.reanalyzeJunk: {{count}} are junk files — suggest removing from the library
settings.reanalyzeClean: All {{scanned}} records already match the new rules
settings.reanalyzeJunkDone: Removed {{count}} records; the files on disk stay where they are
settings.reanalyzeDemote: {{count}} of them are preview images the old rules registered as standalone assets; they will be demoted to attachments
settings.extractRootHint: Where .unitypackage files pulled out of archives are unpacked. Empty = a sibling of the library root (E:\vrc\A → E:\vrc\A__extract). It must not be inside the library or on drive C. Deleted right after use, and pruned again at startup.
settings.extractRootPlaceholder: Empty = automatically use A__extract next to the library root (same drive)
settings.autoSwitchBehaviorHint: What it should do when it notices a Unity project just opened
settings.asbNever: Never — just update the top bar
settings.trayRequiredNote: Atrium can only notice Unity starting while it is running: sitting in the tray is fine, quitting the app stops the auto-switch. “Start with Windows” and “minimise to tray” are two different settings, both above.
settings.autoLaunchAskTitle: Start Atrium with Windows and keep it in the tray?
settings.autoLaunchAskBody: You just opened a Unity project. Atrium has to be running to switch to the matching collection — with start-with-Windows on, it waits in the tray after you log in. Leaving it off is fine too; open Atrium yourself and auto-switching still works.
settings.synonymsHint: Write down what you actually call each kind of asset. Searching “clothes” and getting assets filed under “Clothing” works because of this list, not a hard-coded word table.
settings.synonymsKanjiHint: Japanese kanji names (e.g. 束縛) are not found by their romanisation (sokubaku): that needs a multi-megabyte reading dictionary and still gets polyphonic characters wrong, so it does not do it. Put the original name in the asset notes and it becomes searchable.
settings.synonymsSaved: Saved — the search index was rebuilt to match
settings.synonymDeadWarn: Single-character words are dropped by the search index (too broad) — use two or more

synonym.tooShort: Use at least {{min}} characters — single-character words are thrown away by the index
synonym.tooMany: At most {{max}} nicknames per category — remove a few first

settings.vaultHint: Archives whose password you asked Atrium to keep. The passwords themselves are never shown here — you can only delete them.
settings.vaultUnavailable: System encryption is unavailable on this machine, so nothing new can be stored; entries below may also be unreadable.
settings.vaultUnreadableHint: Happens after moving to another machine or Windows account (the encryption is bound to the current user). This entry is useless now — feel free to delete it.
settings.remerge: Re-merge items that should be one card
settings.remergeFieldHint: Some older entries were filed before the grouping rules changed. The app re-applies today's rules by itself the first time it starts after an update — grouping only, never a file. Use this panel when you want to check again by hand.
settings.remergeHint: Press Check first and see exactly what would merge. Ctrl+Z undoes the whole batch afterwards.
settings.remergeNone: Nothing to re-merge — every group already matches the current rules
settings.remergeScanned: Looked at {{scanned}} cards; {{moved}} of them would move under another card
settings.remergeAmbiguous: {{count}} more look too similar to merge automatically — left for you to decide
settings.remergeDone: Merged: {{clusters}} groups / {{moved}} cards moved / {{groups}} empty groups removed
settings.invalidThreshold: Classification thresholds must be between 0 and 1.
settings.keepOriginalHint: When off, original archives move to undo storage only after extracted files are saved. Unextracted archives and original Unity packages are kept.
settings.confidenceAutoHint: 0–1; automatically archive matches at this threshold when review is not required. Higher is more cautious.
settings.confidenceConfirmHint: 0–1; matches below this threshold require classification review.
settings.databaseBackupHint: Save a complete copy of the current database, including the asset index, classification, collections and import history. Original assets, thumbnails, project files and import file backups are excluded. Saved passwords may not decrypt on another computer.
settings.backupBusy: A database backup is in progress. Please wait.
settings.backupProtectLiveDatabase: Do not overwrite the current database or its journal files. Choose another filename.
settings.backupInvalidTarget: Cannot save the backup here. Choose a valid file path.
settings.backupFailed: Database backup failed. The previous destination file was preserved. Check free space, permissions and file locks.
settings.backupTargetJournal: The destination has database journal files. Choose a new backup filename instead of overwriting it.
settings.unityAutoConnectHint: Prepare the connection when a supported Unity project opens. Install a missing connector once, then wait for Unity before running an import you requested.

health.intro: Scanning is read-only: it touches neither files nor the database. Nothing changes until you press the button on that row.
health.truncated: Too many entries — the scan stopped early, so this is only part of the picture.
health.missingHint: In the database but missing on disk (drive unplugged, or deleted outside Atrium). These get flagged, never deleted.
health.duplicatesHint: Identical content fingerprints (xxh64). Only listed here — which copy to keep is your call.
health.similarHint: Two covers that look almost the same (same image, re-encoded or renamed). Distance 0 means identical.
health.straysHint: Inside the library folder but not in the database. Send them back through the ingest queue as they are.
health.largestHint: Start here if you need space back.
health.orphansHint: A group left with one member (or none) — over-merged. Dissolving tidies it up.
health.dissolved: Dissolved {{count}} groups, {{freed}} assets are standalone again
health.thumbsHint: Remove cached covers no asset references any more (left behind by undo or delete).
health.noLibrary: No library folder set (Settings → Library), so unregistered files cannot be scanned.
health.reclaimNone: Nothing was queued — all {{count}} were refused (already registered, or the folder contains registered assets)
health.autoArchiveNudge: For batched adoption, turn off “Auto-archive confident assets” in Settings → Library first: everything then lands in Review and files only move when you confirm.
health.hasExtracted: {{n}} already-extracted folder(s) with the same name sit next to it (only this archive gets registered; the copy stays put)
health.trashConfirm: Send these {{count}} item(s) to the Recycle Bin? You can restore them there, and the action log keeps a record.

wizard.title: First-time setup
wizard.subtitle: Four steps; change any option later in Settings

step1.title: 1. Where the library lives
step1.body: Choose a dedicated folder for organized assets, separate from your Unity projects.
step1.notFound: That folder is gone (disk unplugged?) — pick another one
step1.warnSystemDrive: It is on C:. Workable, but the library only grows — another drive is usually better.
step1.warnLowFree: Less than 20 GB free on this drive, which may not be enough to unpack big archives.
step1.askTitle: That folder already has assets. What should Atrium do?
step1.adoptBody: Scan and register existing assets, keeping their locations and names. Automatic archiving is turned off.
step1.freshBody: Existing files stay as they are. New assets are saved here by category; an empty folder is recommended.
step1.needRoot: Pick the library folder first (this step cannot be skipped)

facts.unknown: Some subfolders could not be read, so the file count is unknown

step1.unityProject: This folder belongs to a Unity project. Choose a separate asset library folder; connect Unity in a later step.
step1.forbidden: Choose a dedicated asset folder, rather than a drive root or system directory.

step2.title: 2. Where assets come from
step2.body: Watched folders: drop files in and it queues them. Skip it if you like — drag & drop, the Explorer "Send to Atrium" entry and the command line all keep working.
step2.empty: None yet (you can skip this step)

step3.title: ③ Automatic Unity connection (optional)
step3.body: Open a Unity 2022.3 project and Atrium will prepare the connection automatically, installing the connector if it is missing.
step3.none: No running Unity projects found. Open a project to connect automatically, or continue for now.
step3.unknownError: the main process gave no reason
step3.automatic: Connects automatically. No project installation selection is needed. Opening a project does not import assets.

step4.title: 4. Last bits
step4.body: Atrium has to stay in the tray to switch collections the moment Unity starts. Start it with Windows?
step4.launchHint: Changeable any time under Settings → General. Without it Atrium still works — you just have to open it first.

remerge.autoDone: Merged {{moved}} cards that were really the same item ({{clusters}} places)
